implementation_notes: The Go repository is a small interface declared where it is consumed (type InvoiceRepository interface { FindOverdue(ctx, on) ([]Invoice, error) }) plus a struct holding *sql.DB that runs QueryContext/QueryRowContext and scans rows into domain structs. Declaring the interface at the consumer keeps implicit satisfaction working and the implementation free of extra imports; many Go teams stop at query functions in a store package and only introduce the interface when the aggregate must be faked in tests or swapped. Transactions are passed in per call (a *sql.Tx parameter) instead of being held by the repository.
pitfalls: rows must be closed and rows.Err() checked on every path: returning early without Close leaks a pooled connection until the process restarts.
sql.DB is safe for concurrent use, but *sql.Tx is not: never store a transaction in a long-lived repository struct - pass it per call so goroutines cannot share it.
The nil-interface trap: returning a typed nil (*InvoiceRepo)(nil) as the interface yields a non-nil interface value, so callers and tests invoke methods on a nil receiver.

variants.name: sqlc-generated queries behind the same interface
variants.idiom_name: sqlc-generated *Queries wrapped by a thin adapter
variants.implementation_notes: Write the SQL in .sql files and let sqlc generate typed Go functions; the repository becomes a thin adapter that implements the domain interface by calling the generated methods and converting generated row structs into domain structs. SQL stays reviewable and typed, Scan code disappears, and the adapter keeps generated types out of the domain. Regenerate as part of the build so schema and queries cannot drift.
pitfalls: Generated row structs must not leak into the domain: convert at the adapter, otherwise every schema change becomes a domain change.
Generated code is only correct for the pinned sqlc version: pin the tool (tools.go / go.mod) so a regeneration in CI cannot silently rewrite query semantics.
sqlc makes dynamic queries awkward: a highly conditional query becomes many SQL statements or a hand-written builder, which argues for keeping such reads outside the repository interface.
